_readme: Fixtures for scripts/verify_context_declaration.py (tests/test_context_declaration_lint.py). 'divergent' declares a path (references/narrowed-away.md) that never appears in its task's imperative prose -- a declaration pointing somewhere its own prose never covers -- and must be REJECTED. 'prose_names_more_than_declared' is the opposite shape: the prose names a file (docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md) that the declaration quietly omits -- the declaration silently narrowing away from what the prose describes -- and the lint cannot see this direction, so it must PASS. 'valid' declares only paths that do appear verbatim, and must PASS. 'boundary_suffix_rejected' declares 'agents/GLOSSARY.md' where the prose only ever names the longer, different path 'docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md' -- a bare substring match would wrongly pass this; the boundary rule must REJECT it (leading side). 'boundary_legitimate_occurrences_accepted' declares five paths, each occurring in the prose at a different legitimate leading boundary (start-of-string, preceded by whitespace, by a backtick, by '(', and by a quote) -- all must PASS. 'boundary_trailing_rejected' declares 'docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md' where the prose only ever names the longer, different path 'docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md.bak' (a realistic backup-sibling drift shape) -- must REJECT it (trailing side). 'boundary_trailing_legitimate_accepted' declares five paths, each occurring in the prose immediately before a different legitimate trailing boundary (a sentence-ending period, a comma, a closing backtick, a closing paren, and end-of-string) -- all must PASS, proving the trailing rule does not over-reject the real prose shapes this repo's templates actually use (the shipped COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json ends several of its own declared paths in a sentence period). All are full gated-checklist shapes so the lint runs unmodified over real spine JSON.
